title: The small affine etale site computes the etale topos and its cohomology
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with small etale site $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $S_{affine,\Et}$ be the site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] whose underlying category is the full subcategory of $S_{\Et}$ of the $U\to S$ with $U$ affine, and whose coverings are the standard etale coverings $\{U_j\to U\}_{j=1,\dots,m}$: finite families with every $U_j$ affine and etale over $U$ and $U=\bigcup_jf_j(U_j)$ (Stacks Topologies, Definitions 0219 and 021B(4)). Then the inclusion $\iota:S_{affine,\Et}\to S_{\Et}$ is special cocontinuous and induces an equivalence of topoi: restriction $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G|_{S_{affine,\Et}}=\mathcal G\circ\iota$ is an equivalence from abelian sheaves on $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] to abelian sheaves on $S_{affine,\Et}$ (and likewise for sheaves of sets) (Topologies, Lemma 04HR). Moreover, for every abelian sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $S_{\Et}$ and every object $U$ of $S_{affine,\Et}$ there are isomorphisms $H^p(U,\mathcal G|_{S_{affine,\Et}})\cong H^p(U,\mathcal G)$ ($p\ge0$; left side cohomology over $U$ on the site $S_{affine,\Et}$, right side on $S_{\Et}$, [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]), functorial in $\mathcal G$, and equal to the identity of $\mathcal G(U)$ for $p=0$; for $U=S$ affine the right side is $H^p(S_{\Et},\mathcal G)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: *$S_{affine,\Et}$ is a site.* Write $\mathcal C=S_{affine,\Et}$ (objects the etale $U\to S$ with $U$ affine [def-pc-scheme], morphisms the $S$-morphisms, a full subcategory of $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]) and $\iota:\mathcal C\to S_{\Et}$ for the inclusion. (i) Fibre products: for morphisms $V\to U\leftarrow W$ in $\mathcal C$ the scheme-theoretic fibre product $V\times_UW$ with its map to $S$ is etale over $S$ and is a fibre product in $S_{\Et}$ ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](2)); it is affine, since $U,V,W$ are affine and a fibre product of affine schemes over an affine scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the tensor product ([lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], after choosing isomorphisms $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$, $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$, $W\cong\operatorname{Spec}C$ and using that a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a ring map, [def-weil-affine-spectrum]); as $\mathcal C$ is full, $V\times_UW$ is a fibre product in $\mathcal C$, and $\iota$ preserves fibre products. (ii) Site axioms for the standard etale coverings (finite families $\{U_j\to U\}$ of morphisms of $\mathcal C$ with $U=\bigcup_jf_j(U_j)$; each $U_j\to U$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](3), being an $S$-morphism between schemes etale over $S$): an isomorphism $\{V\xrightarrow{\sim}U\}$ is a finite jointly surjective family of affines, hence standard; if $\{U_j\to U\}_{j\le m}$ and, for each $j$, $\{U_{jk}\to U_j\}_{k\le m_j}$ are standard, then $\{U_{jk}\to U\}$ is finite, consists of affines, and is jointly surjective (a point of $U$ is the image of a point of some $U_j$, which is the image of a point of some $U_{jk}$), so it is standard; if $\{U_j\to U\}$ is standard and $T\to U$ is a morphism of $\mathcal C$, then $\{U_j\times_UT\to T\}$ is finite, its members are objects of $\mathcal C$ by (i), and it is jointly surjective with etale members by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], so it is standard. Hence $\mathcal C$ with the standard etale coverings is a site in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1), with fibre products computed in $S_{\Et}$.

proof.text: *$\iota$ is special cocontinuous.* We check conditions (a)-(e) of [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor] (Stacks Sites, Lemma 03A0 (1)-(5)), following the proof of Topologies Lemma 021E. (a) Cocontinuity: let $U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and let $\{V_k\to\iota(U)\}_{k\in K}$ be a covering of $S_{\Et}$, i.e. a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms. Since $U$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-affine-refinement] gives finitely many affine open subschemes $U_j\subseteq V_{k(j)}$ whose images cover $U$; the open immersion $U_j\hookrightarrow V_{k(j)}$ is etale and composites of etale morphisms are etale ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2)), so $U_j\to U$ and $U_j\to U\to S$ are etale, $U_j\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$, $\{U_j\to U\}$ is a standard etale covering of $\mathcal C$, and each $\iota(U_j)\to\iota(U)$ factors through $V_{k(j)}\to\iota(U)$: the family refines the given covering. (b) Continuity: a standard etale covering $\{U_j\to U\}$ is a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms, hence a covering of $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and for $T\to U$ in $\mathcal C$ the morphisms $\iota(U_j\times_UT)\to\iota(U_j)\times_{\iota(U)}\iota(T)$ are isomorphisms because fibre products of $\mathcal C$ are those of $S_{\Et}$ (step 1); this is continuity in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3). (c) If $a,b:U'\to U$ in $\mathcal C$ have $\iota(a)=\iota(b)$ then $a=b$ ($\iota$ is the inclusion of a subcategory), and the covering $\{\mathrm{id}_{U'}\}$ works. (d) Given $U',U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $c:\iota(U')\to\iota(U)$ in $S_{\Et}$, $c$ is a morphism of $\mathcal C$ ($\mathcal C$ is full); take the covering $\{\mathrm{id}_{U'}\}$ and $c_1=c$. (e) Let $V\to S$ be an object of $S_{\Et}$. $V$ is covered by affine open subschemes $V_k$ (every scheme is locally affine, [def-pc-scheme]); the open immersions $V_k\hookrightarrow V$ [def-weil-open-immersion] are etale and $V_k\to V\to S$ is etale ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2)), so $V_k\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $\{\iota(V_k)\to V\}$ is a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms, a covering of $S_{\Et}$. Hence $\iota$ is special cocontinuous.

source.place: Proof of Lemma Tag 021E (label lemma-affine-big-site-etale), adapted to the small sites as the hint of Lemma Tag 04HR says; Lemma Tag 0218 (label lemma-etale-affine) for (a); conditions of literature/stacks-project/sites.tex Lemma Tag 03A0 (label lemma-equivalence)

proof.text: *The standard etale topology on $\mathcal C$ is the topology induced from $S_{\Et}$.* Let $J_{\mathrm{std}}$ be the Grothendieck topology on $\mathcal C$ generated by the standard etale coverings (a sieve $R$ on $U$ is covering iff it contains the members of a standard etale covering of $U$), and $J_{\Et}$ the one on $S_{\Et}$ generated by the jointly surjective etale families. Both families of coverings satisfy the site axioms (step 1, [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]) and both categories have fibre products, so by [lem-weil-pbc-pretopology-sheaf-condition] the sheaves of sets, resp. of abelian groups, on the site $\mathcal C$ are exactly the $J_{\mathrm{std}}$-sheaves, and the sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], resp. abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], on $S_{\Et}$ are exactly the $J_{\Et}$-sheaves. Claim: for a sieve $R$ on $U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$, $R\in J_{\mathrm{std}}(U)$ iff the sieve $\iota R$ on $\iota(U)$ generated by the morphisms $\iota(r)$, $r\in R$, lies in $J_{\Et}(\iota U)$; that is, $J_{\mathrm{std}}$ is the topology induced by $\iota$ from $J_{\Et}$. If $R$ contains the members of a standard covering $\{U_j\to U\}$, these form a covering of $S_{\Et}$ (step 2(b)) whose members lie in $\iota R$, so $\iota R\in J_{\Et}(\iota U)$. Conversely, if $\iota R\in J_{\Et}(\iota U)$, it contains the members of a jointly surjective etale family $\{V_k\to\iota(U)\}$; by step 2(a) there is a standard covering $\{g_j:U_j\to U\}$ such that each $g_j$ factors as $U_j\xrightarrow{h_j}V_{k(j)}\to\iota(U)$; as $V_{k(j)}\to\iota(U)$ lies in $\iota R$ it factors as $V_{k(j)}\xrightarrow{w}\iota(W)\xrightarrow{\iota(r)}\iota(U)$ with $r:W\to U$ in $R$; then $w\circ h_j:U_j\to W$ is a morphism between objects of $\mathcal C$, hence of $\mathcal C$ ($\mathcal C$ full), and $g_j=r\circ(w\circ h_j)\in R$ because $R$ is a sieve. So $R$ contains a standard covering and $R\in J_{\mathrm{std}}(U)$.

proof.text: *Restriction is an equivalence (sets and abelian groups).* Let $\mathcal V$ be the category of sets or of abelian groups. Let $\mathcal A_S$ (pairs $(R,f)$, $f:\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$ etale) and $P:\mathcal A_S\to S_{\Et}$ be as in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-induced-sheaf-equivalence], with the topology $T_P$ induced by $P$. Define $e:\mathcal A_S\to\mathcal C$ by $e(R,f)=(\operatorname{Spec}R\xrightarrow{f}S)$ and $e(g)=g$; then $\iota\circ e=P$. $e$ is fully faithful (in both categories a morphism is an $S$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$) and essentially surjective: an object $U\to S$ of $\mathcal C$ has $U$ affine, so there is an isomorphism $\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}A\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ [def-pc-scheme], the composite $f=(U\to S)\circ\varphi$ is etale ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2), an isomorphism being an open immersion), and $\varphi:e(A,f)\to U$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal C$. So $e$ is an equivalence of categories. For a sieve $R$ on $c\in\mathcal A_S$, the sieve on $P(c)=\iota(e(c))$ generated by the $P(r)=\iota(e(r))$ is the sieve $\iota(eR)$ generated by $\iota$ of the sieve $eR$ generated by the $e(r)$ (both consist of the morphisms factoring through some $\iota(e(r))$); hence by step 3, $R\in T_P(c)$ iff $eR\in J_{\mathrm{std}}(e(c))$, i.e. $T_P$ is the topology induced by $e$ from $J_{\mathrm{std}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-sheaf-transport] (applied to $e:\mathcal A_S\to\mathcal C$, $J=J_{\mathrm{std}}$, $K=T_P$), $\mathrm{Res}_e:\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F\circ e$ is an equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C,J_{\mathrm{std}};\mathcal V)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal A_S,T_P;\mathcal V)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-induced-sheaf-equivalence], $\mathrm{Res}_P:\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G\circ P$ is an equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\Et};\mathcal V)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal A_S,T_P;\mathcal V)$. The restriction $\mathrm{Res}_\iota:\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G\circ\iota$ carries sheaves on $S_{\Et}$ to sheaves on $\mathcal C$ (for a standard covering $\{U_j\to U\}$, a covering of $S_{\Et}$ whose fibre products are computed in $S_{\Et}$ (steps 1, 2(b)), the equalizer diagram of $\mathcal G\circ\iota$ is that of $\mathcal G$; this is $u^s$ of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3)), and $\mathrm{Res}_P=\mathrm{Res}_e\circ\mathrm{Res}_\iota$ because $P=\iota\circ e$. With a quasi-inverse $Q_e$ of $\mathrm{Res}_e$ we get $\mathrm{Res}_\iota\cong Q_e\circ\mathrm{Res}_e\circ\mathrm{Res}_\iota=Q_e\circ\mathrm{Res}_P$, a composite of equivalences, so $\mathrm{Res}_\iota$ is an equivalence (a functor isomorphic to an equivalence is one). By step 3 the source and target are the categories of sheaves of $\mathcal V$ on $S_{\Et}$ and on the site $S_{affine,\Et}$ of the statement. This proves the equivalence of topoi (sheaves of sets) and of the categories of abelian sheaves $\Ab(S_{\Et})\to\Ab(S_{affine,\Et})$, $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G|_{S_{affine,\Et}}$. (This is the conclusion of Stacks Sites Lemma 03A0 for the special cocontinuous $\iota$ of step 2: the morphism of topoi of $\iota$ has inverse image $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G\circ\iota$.)

proof.text: *Cohomology over an affine $U$.* Write $\Phi=\mathrm{Res}_\iota:\Ab(S_{\Et})\to\Ab(\mathcal C)$, $\Phi(\mathcal G)=\mathcal G|_{S_{affine,\Et}}$. Both categories are abelian with enough injectives ([def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]); $\Phi$ is additive ($(\varphi+\psi)\circ\iota=\varphi\circ\iota+\psi\circ\iota$, sums of morphisms of sheaves being taken sectionwise) and an equivalence (step 4). Let $U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $\mathcal G\in\Ab(S_{\Et})$; choose an injective resolution $s:\mathcal G\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ in $\Ab(S_{\Et})$ ([lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero](1)). By [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions](3), $\Phi(s):\Phi\mathcal G\to\Phi\mathcal I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution in $\Ab(\mathcal C)$. Since $\Gamma(U,\Phi\mathcal I^q)=\mathcal I^q(\iota U)=\Gamma(\iota U,\mathcal I^q)$ with the same differentials, the definition of cohomology over an object [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](2) (computed with any injective resolution, up to canonical isomorphism) gives $H^p(U,\mathcal G|_{S_{affine,\Et}})=H^p(\Gamma(U,\Phi\mathcal I^\bullet))=H^p(\Gamma(\iota U,\mathcal I^\bullet))=H^p(U,\mathcal G)$. Independence and functoriality: if $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ and $\varphi^\bullet:\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal I'^\bullet$ is a morphism of injective resolutions lifting it (unique up to homotopy), then $\Phi(\varphi^\bullet)$ lifts $\Phi(\varphi)$ and a homotopy goes to a homotopy ([lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions](3)), and $\Gamma(U,\Phi\varphi^\bullet)=\Gamma(\iota U,\varphi^\bullet)$; so the maps induced on $H^p$ by $\varphi$ on both sides correspond under the identification (with $\varphi=\mathrm{id}$ this shows the identification does not depend on the chosen resolution), i.e. the isomorphisms are functorial in $\mathcal G$. For $p=0$ both sides are identified with sections through the augmentation, $H^0(U,\Phi\mathcal G)\cong\Phi\mathcal G(U)$ and $H^0(U,\mathcal G)\cong\mathcal G(\iota U)$ ([lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero](2) for the left exact functors $\Gamma(U,-)$, $\Gamma(\iota U,-)$), and $\Phi(s)(U)=s(\iota U)$, so the isomorphism in degree $0$ is the identity of $\mathcal G(U)=\Phi\mathcal G(U)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03YU (label lemma-cohomology-bigger-site) and its proof: sections over corresponding objects agree and injectives go to injectives (here because Phi is an equivalence, Homology Lemma 015Z applied to Phi and its quasi-inverse)

proof.text: *The case $U=S$ affine.* The object $\mathrm{id}_S:S\to S$ is a final object of $S_{\Et}$ ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](2)) and $\Gamma(S,-)$ is evaluation at it. The etale cohomology $H^p(S_{\Et},\mathcal G)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] is $\mathcal H^p(\Gamma(S,\mathcal K^\bullet))$ for a K-injective resolution $\mathcal G\to\mathcal K^\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. An injective resolution $\mathcal G\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a bounded below complex of injectives, hence K-injective, and two K-injective resolutions of $\mathcal G$ are chain homotopy equivalent compatibly with the augmentations, functorially up to homotopy ([prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]); so $H^p(S_{\Et},\mathcal G)=H^p(\Gamma(S,\mathcal I^\bullet))=H^p(S,\mathcal G)$, cohomology over the final object in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](2), canonically and functorially in $\mathcal G$. If $S$ is affine, $S\to S$ is an object of $S_{affine,\Et}$ and step 5 with $U=S$ gives $H^p(S,\mathcal G|_{S_{affine,\Et}})\cong H^p(S_{\Et},\mathcal G)$, functorially in $\mathcal G$.
